original_question: Let F be a family of subsets of [n] that is diamond-free as an induced poset and maximal with respect to that property, meaning that adjoining any set outside F creates an induced diamond. Determine whether every such diamond-saturated family must have size Omega(n).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s poset-saturation question: a family F of subsets of [n] that avoids an induced diamond, is maximal under adding any new set, and the problem of whether every such family must have linear size in n.
missing_details: The ambient universe should be stated explicitly: [n] = {1,2,...,n} and F is a subfamily of the Boolean lattice 2^[n].

The induced diamond condition should be given exactly: F contains no four distinct sets A, B, C, D with A ⊂ B ∩ C, B ∪ C ⊂ D, and B ⊄ C and C ⊄ B; this encodes that the middle two sets are incomparable.
Maximality should be quantified over every X in 2^[n] \ F: for each such X, the family F ∪ {X} contains an induced diamond.
The asymptotic meaning of Ω(n) should be unpacked: there should exist constants c > 0 and n0 such that every such family F satisfies |F| ≥ c n for all n ≥ n0.
The paper uses the term 'diamond-saturated' for exactly the conjunction of induced-diamond-freeness and maximality, so that terminology can be included explicitly.
refined_question: Let [n] = {1,2,...,n}, and let F ⊆ 2^[n]. Suppose that F contains no induced copy of the diamond poset; equivalently, there do not exist four distinct sets A, B, C, D ∈ F such that A ⊂ B ∩ C, B ∪ C ⊂ D, and B ⊄ C and C ⊄ B. Suppose further that F is maximal with respect to this property, in the sense that for every X ∈ 2^[n] \ F, the family F ∪ {X} does contain such an induced diamond. Must there exist constants c > 0 and n0 such that every such family F satisfies |F| ≥ c n for all n ≥ n0?
justification: In arXiv:2310.18163, your draft matches Question 7.3 in Section 7 essentially exactly. The nearby text in the same section supplies the precise induced-diamond configuration, names such families 'diamond-saturated', and states the intended level of the open problem: whether every diamond-saturated family has linear size. The same context also notes examples of size n + 1 and records the currently known lower-bound landscape, so the faithful refinement should remain narrowly focused on this linear lower-bound question rather than broaden to other saturation variants.
